## 1. One method for any tool

ISO 26262-8 §11 qualifies a tool **for a use case**, not a product. The same five steps apply to a commercial
requirements tool such as DOORS, Jama or Polarion, to a compiler, and to a script written for this project. What
decides the outcome is not the tool's name or price but the guards around it: the measures that would catch the
tool's errors before they reach the product.

| Step | Question | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Use case | What does the tool do here, on which element, and what would an error look like? | A use case and its error classes (§4) |
| 2. Tool impact (TI) | Can an error put a fault into a safety-related element, or fail to detect one? | TI1 or TI2 |
| 3. Guards and TD | Which guards of the [catalogue](guards.yaml) catch each error class, and is each shown working? | TD1, TD2 or TD3 (§3) |
| 4. TCL | TI1, or TI2 with TD1, gives TCL1. TI2 with TD2 gives TCL2, and TI2 with TD3 gives TCL3 | TCL1 needs nothing more |
| 5. Method and report | For TCL2 and TCL3: which method the standard names (1a increased confidence from use, 1b evaluation of the tool development process, 1c validation of the software tool, 1d development to a safety standard), and the evidence it produces | A tool qualification report (TQR), re-run when its triggers fire (§6) |

The classification of every tool is in WP-P-07 §3. The reports are in this folder.

## 2. Why the guards decide

Two tools in the same use case get the same TCL when the same guards surround them. A requirements tool at TCL1 is
TCL1 because a review, a check or a second tool catches its errors, not because it is a well-known product. Swap the
tool and keep the guards, and its classification holds. Remove a guard, and even a well-known tool loses TD1.

So this project can use any tool, a commercial one or its own, provided the guards for its error classes are in
place and shown working. A guard counts only once it is shown working: a planted-fault suite that runs in CI is
shown working, while a review that has no named reviewer is not.

## 3. From guards to TD

This is the project's rule for step 3. It is a rule for this project, applied the same way to every tool. The
standard asks for confidence that errors are prevented or detected; it does not prescribe this rule.

| TD | When |
|---|---|
| TD1 (high) | Every error class of the use case is caught by at least one guard that is independent of the tool and shown working on every change (TG-02, TG-03 or TG-06 in CI, or TG-05 with a named reviewer) |
| TD2 (medium) | Every error class has a guard, but at least one is not independent of the tool, not shown working, or runs only at a baseline |
| TD3 (low) | At least one error class has no guard |

A planted-fault suite (TG-01) is a special case. It shows that the tool catches each planted error pattern, in the
version it ran on, and so it is the evidence of method 1c (validation of the software tool). It does not catch an
error on an input pattern nobody planted, so on its own it does not raise TD. TD comes from the guards that check the
tool's real output in use: a second tool, a recomputation, a round trip or a review.

## 4. Error classes of requirements management and traceability

These are the errors that matter for any tool that holds safety requirements and their links: DOORS, Jama, Polarion,
or this project's YAML items checked by [`check_trace.py`](../../trace/tools/check_trace.py). A report for such a
tool shows how each class is caught.

| Class | The tool lets this through |
|---|---|
| EC-1 Broken link | A link to an item that does not exist, or to the wrong kind of item |
| EC-2 Orphan | A requirement, hazard or AI requirement that rests on nothing |
| EC-3 Missing refinement | A goal, requirement, hazard or threat that nothing refines or covers |
| EC-4 ASIL not inherited | A requirement rated below what it refines, without a recorded decomposition |
| EC-5 Wrong ASIL | An ASIL that does not follow from its risk parameters or its sources |
| EC-6 Identity | Two items with one ID, or an ID outside the scheme |
| EC-7 Missing attribute | A mandatory attribute missing, or a status outside the lifecycle |
| EC-8 Test link | A test linked to a requirement that does not exist or is withdrawn |
| EC-9 Copy differs from the record | The tool's copy of a requirement differs from the work product it came from |
| EC-10 Status without evidence | An item marked agreed or accepted without the review that makes it so |

## 5. What a report holds

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Header | Tool, exact version, use case, TI, TD, TCL, method, status |
| Use case | What the tool does and the error that matters |
| Guards | Which guards of the catalogue apply, for which error class, and how each is shown working |
| Validation | For method 1c: the fault catalogue, the tool mutants and the results, generated and checked in CI |
| Use constraints | Allowed options and known limitations, which reviewers check ([WP-P-05](../WP-P-05-verification-review-procedure.md)) |
| Re-qualification | The triggers of §6 that apply |
| Acceptance | Who accepts the result (the lead, through the decision register), the independent review, the assessor |

## 6. When a report is run again

| Trigger | What happens |
|---|---|
| Any change to the tool, its fault catalogue or the records it reads | CI runs the validation on every change; a missed fault, a surviving mutant or a stale result fails the run |
| A new check in the tool | The test of the qualification fails until the catalogue has a fault for it |
| A new version of a pinned dependency | The run fails until the new version is re-run and recorded (WP-P-07 §6) |
| A new use case, or credit taken where none was | Classify again (WP-P-07 §3) and extend the report |

## 7. What stays with people

The tooling shows that a guard works. It does not accept the result. Three things stay with people:

- **The lead** accepts each report through the [decision register](../../01-management/decisions/register.yaml).
- **An independent reviewer** reviews each in-house tool as test software (WP-P-07 OI-13).
- **The assessor** samples the reports in the confirmation review of WP-P-07 (CR-09, [WP-M-06](../../01-management/WP-M-06-confirmation-measures-plan.md)).
